title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 220 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $17,445.07 and a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes. Team Beta carries the highest labor cost share. Email tickets reopen at more than twice the rate of chat tickets. A small high-cost, low-satisfaction segment of 9 tickets warrants targeted intervention. Agent workload is moderately concentrated, with the busiest agent handling 7.3% of all tickets.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 220 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.7 minutes and a total labor cost of $17,445.07.
Team Beta incurred the highest labor cost at $6,928.72, followed by Gamma at $5,911.44 and Alpha at $4,604.91. Beta accounts for the largest share of total labor spend.
Chat had the longest mean resolution time at 82.2 minutes, followed by phone at 74.1 minutes and email at 71.7 minutes.
Email tickets reopen at 15.2%, compared to 6.8% for chat — an increase of 122.5% relative to the chat rate, indicating email is a materially higher-risk channel for reopening.
Nine tickets met the high-cost (labor_cost ≥ $100) and low-satisfaction (score ≤ 2) criteria, with 11.1% of them having been reopened — a segment meriting priority review.

Resolution times show a median of 65.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.3 minutes, indicating notable spread. Mean satisfaction among scored tickets is 4.1 out of 5, with 14 tickets missing a satisfaction score.
Across 18 distinct agents, the busiest single agent handled 16 tickets, representing 7.3% of total volume — a moderate concentration with no single agent dominating the workload.

limitations: Both the cleaning and analysis pipeline stages reported validation failures; results should be treated as provisional until the underlying data quality issues are investigated and resolved.
Fourteen tickets are missing satisfaction scores, which may introduce bias into the satisfaction mean if missingness is non-random.
The high-cost, low-satisfaction segment contains only 9 tickets, making the 11.1% reopen rate statistically fragile and sensitive to individual cases.
Labor cost calculations depend on the accuracy of the agent roster join; any unmatched records dropped during cleaning could distort team-level cost comparisons.
The analysis covers a single export snapshot with no time dimension, so trends over time cannot be assessed.
conclusion: Support operations show broadly acceptable performance — a mean satisfaction of 4.1 and moderate agent concentration — but two areas require attention: email's reopen rate is 122% higher than chat's, and a small cluster of expensive, low-satisfaction tickets has an elevated reopen rate. Resolving the pipeline validation failures is a prerequisite before acting on these figures with high confidence.
